title: Categories goes back to Name A to Z after you leave and come back
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919), with the Settings - Parts permission.
  • Category {Category-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PCA01 alpha) exists.
  • Category {Category-B} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PCA01 Beta) exists.
  • You are on a page other than Categories.
custom_steps:
1. Go to Settings and click Categories in the Parts group of the Settings menu.
  2. Click the Name column header once.
  3. Move the mouse pointer away from the column headers.
  4. Read the Name header arrow and the order of {Category-A} and {Category-B}.
  5. Click Pricing in the Parts group of the Settings menu.
  6. Go to Settings and click Categories in the Parts group of the Settings menu.
  7. Move the mouse pointer away from the column headers.
  8. Read the Name header arrow and the order of {Category-A} and {Category-B}.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 4: the Name header arrow points down and {Category-B} is above {Category-A} (Z to A).
  • Step 8: the Name header arrow points up again and {Category-A} is above {Category-B} (A to Z). The sort from step 2 was not kept.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-11258; story SV-10134 (Story 1, Categories, sort by name; story text re-synced to the PRD on 13 Oct 2026); PRD "Settings Pricing And Categories Sorting (Price/Category)", Confluence 578781186, version 21 (14 Oct 2026), S1-R16, §5 Terminology 'Fresh open', read 14 Oct 2026; design canvas board 1.2 (Categories - after), 13 Oct copy, unchanged on 14 Oct. Source-verified 14 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Price/Category QA build exists).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S1-R16: “Opening the page afresh returns the list to name ascending, whatever sort was applied last time.”
  • PRD Story 1 context note: “Navigating away and returning is a fresh open, which is S1-R16.”
  • PRD §5 Terminology: “Fresh open - the user arrives at the page again, having been somewhere else.”
